name: Overhead extension
cue: Keep your elbows by your ears and straighten your arms up.
research: research.json biomech.overhead_ext: facing away from the cable column in a staggered stance (left foot forward: hip 40 pelvis-relative / 45 trunk-relative, knee 25, ankle 15; right leg behind nearly straight with the heel lifted, metatarsal heads pinned, toes flat), trunk leaning 35 deg (pelvis 30, lumbar 3, thorax 2), core braced. Upper arms beside the head at shoulder flexion ~160 -> 155 (35 deg above horizontal in the world), elbows shoulder-width, not flared. Elbow 140 -> 5: a short straight bar travels an arc on a hinge at the elbow line (tools/design/overhead_ext.mjs, leverFit), from behind the head at upper-neck level to straight arms in front of the head. The pulley is set high (1.18 H, 2.1 m) behind the lifter (research: "a high pulley also works with more lean"; the lean is the researched 35 deg). Deviation from "arms straight and in line with the cable": with a single cable to the middle of the bar, the arm line extended backward runs through the shoulders and head, so the cable cannot be in line with the arms at lockout without passing through the head. At the earlier 1.08 H the cable passed just over the crown at lockout (6.6 cm in 3D, but only a few pixels on the phone, so it read as resting on the head); at 1.18 H it clears the head by 9 cm and visibly runs above it on the phone, while the stretch (hands behind the upper neck, cable 4.7 cm from the head) is unchanged. A higher pulley also keeps the cable across the forearm at the stretch, so the long head is loaded there (cable moment arm at the stretch 0.056 H at 1.08, larger higher up; 0.030 at 1.0 and 0.013 at 0.95). Overhand grip on the bar (hand pro 180: palms up behind the head, palms forward-down at lockout); the bar hinge axis is pure X so both hands stay on the bar symmetrically, and its pivot sits 0.001 H from the FK elbow toward the shoulder so the arms end at ~7 deg instead of overreaching. Scapulohumeral rhythm (BRIEF 2, about 2:1 beyond 30 deg): with the humerus held ~160 deg overhead through the rep, the shoulder girdle proxy (clavicle elevation, standing for scapular upward rotation in this rig) is held at 22 deg (was 8), so about 22 of the ~160 deg read-back elevation comes from the girdle. The exact 2:1 split (about 45 deg of scapular rotation at 165 deg of elevation) cannot be drawn with this rig: its only girdle degree of freedom is clavicle elevation about the SC joint, which lifts the shoulder joint straight up (about 7 cm at 28 deg, 12 cm at 45) and reads as the hard shrug the research lists as a mistake; about 22 deg is the most it shows as upward rotation without a visible shrug (front view checked). So the drawn split is about 5:1 beyond 30 deg; a true 2:1 needs a scapula bone that rotates about the AC joint (engine change, owner call). The arm keys keep the same thorax-frame humerus and forearm (read-back unchanged), and the bar hinge and bar moved with the raised shoulders (+0.018 H up, +0.013 H forward; refit with tools/fk.mjs). The raised bar also lifts the cable a little further off the crown at lockout.

camera.note: Research view az 90 / el 5 (profile: the lean, the upper arms beside the head, the deep elbow bend and the cable from behind). Turned 15 deg toward the front and lowered 5 deg: the triceps face down-forward on the raised upper arms, so this shows both arms' triceps along their length instead of only the near arm's edge.
